To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability of software systems is a function of the reliability of the hardware on which the software is running, and that the reliability of the software is a function of how the system is designed.

(1) the reliability of software is not a function of time, (2) the reliability of a software system can be predicted by using the software's failure rate, (3) software reliability can be increased by using structured programming techniques, (4) the reliability of the software system is a function of the reliability of the components that make up the system, (5) the reliability of hardware and software components can be increased by the use of redundant components.

the following factors are the most important in determining reliability: (1) the quality of the requirements definition process, (2) the quality of design and implementation methodology, (3) the quality of testing, (4) the amount of time available to develop the software, (5) the quality of management, (6) the quality of software tools and (7) the amount and quality of the software documentation.
